annotations.text:
KinEMOS P1 — the study room.

Four states of one surface, drawn in EMOS's real tokens (IBM Plex, #185FA5, 4/8/12/16/24 spacing).

Every number is a plausible sample, not a measurement — rearrange freely, they carry no meaning yet.

The open question on this board:

Numbers live in the RIGHT rail, charts along the BOTTOM. The alternative is numbers under the video and the right rail given to reps/history.

Which do you look at more while judging a lift?

The confidence strip under the video is my proposal, not something you asked for: it tells you WHICH frames to check instead of making you scrub all 218.

Worth building, or noise?

Comparison hinges on the alignment anchor — first frame / bar off floor / start of second pull.

I defaulted to second pull. If a coach's eye actually starts at the floor, that default is wrong.

Calibration is drawn as step 1 of 3 (calibrate → track → phases).

If you'd rather it be a panel you can reopen any time instead of a gate at the start, say so — that changes the whole flow.
